design.decision: Each [2] is a guaranteed trick you can time freely: follow with it to steal an opponent's [A], or keep it for the last trick. A nil bidder must never play their [2]s, which turns the safest nil card into the most dangerous one.
design.opponent: Revealed the first time a [2] beats a trump; opponents can't stop it, so they bid around it and try to strand the [2]s by never leading those suits.
design.rationale: A memorable rule bender: the lowest card becomes the strongest. On its own it adds about two sure tricks per round, so it is worth buying before you know your build. With uc-low-to-twos it becomes a broken combo that needs luck, which the brief allows. It is kept to [2]s only so it stays one short sentence and stays distinct from rc-low-beats.
design.draftText: Your team's [2]s win every trick they are played to
design.hooks: Extend the 'beats' rule with an option to beat trump too (over: trump): the matching cards beat every card in the trick, not only their own suit; ties between two such cards go to the first one played. General for any filter.

critic.concerns: Opponents can't answer a [2] except by stranding it, and a nil bidder forced to follow with a [2] busts automatically; memorable and fully rules-evaluable.
